input.command: ls; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | grep -v '.git/' | head -50; cat -n src/api.ts

input.reason: In src/api.ts, `json()` (line 7) throws on any non-2xx status. `fetchCurrentUser` (line 13) returns that promise without a catch, and `loadDashboard` awaits it at line 27 with no try/catch. The only caller, `mountDashboard` in src/dashboard.ts:5, calls `void loadDashboard(...)`. It attaches no `.catch` and shows no error UI, so any rejection is dropped. The root element keeps showing "Loading..." and `render` is never called. The issue is confirmed at src/api.ts:13 and src/api.ts:27. One part of F03 is wrong: `fetchUserList` (lines 16-24) cannot reject. It returns [] when `!res.ok` and has a catch-all that returns [], so only `fetchCurrentUser` can make the dashboard load fail. F03's main defect, an unhandled rejection in loadDashboard that stops the render, still holds, so it is on topic.
input.failure_scenario: A user's session expires and GET /api/me returns 401, or the request fails with a network error. `json()` throws `HTTP 401`, so `fetchCurrentUser` rejects and `loadDashboard` rejects at src/api.ts:27 before it calls `render`. `mountDashboard` discards the promise with `void`. The page stays on "Loading..." with no error message and no retry, and the browser logs an unhandled promise rejection.
input.severity_reason: The bug only shows up when /api/me fails, such as an expired session, a server error or a network drop. That is an error path, not the normal load path. When it happens, the dashboard hangs on "Loading..." with no feedback to the user. Nothing is corrupted and there is no security impact, so this is wrong behavior on an edge case, not on a common path.
